# Colophon {.unnumbered}

This book was produced with [Quarto](https://quarto.org).
Its examples use R, the `zzcollab` framework, Docker, and
`renv`, each introduced in the chapter that first requires
it.

The book is built as a Quarto project, and the sources
render to HTML and PDF with `quarto render`. Wherever we
present a computed figure or table, that result was
produced by executing the code shown beside it, not typed
by hand. It was not necessarily produced by the build
that made this copy. The book renders with Quarto's
`freeze: auto` setting, under which a page's code is
re-executed only when that page's source file changes;
otherwise the results stored in the freeze cache at its
last execution are replayed. A change to a package
version, a data file, or a function under `R/` does not
by itself trigger re-execution. A printed result
therefore agrees with the code beside it as of that
page's last execution. The table below follows the same
discipline: every cell in the 'Actual' column is read from
the R session that last executed this page, and every cell
in the 'Locked' column from the committed `renv.lock`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-colophon
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: 'The rendering environment of the last execution of this page, read from the live session, beside the versions the committed lockfile records.'

pkg_deps <- c('tibble', 'ggplot2', 'withr', 'knitr',
              'rmarkdown')

pkg_versions <- vapply(pkg_deps, function(p) {
  if (requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    as.character(utils::packageVersion(p))
  } else {
    'not loaded'
  }
}, character(1))

lockfile_path <- file.path('..', '..', 'renv.lock')
lockfile_present <- file.exists(lockfile_path)
dockerfile_present <- file.exists(
  file.path('..', '..', 'Dockerfile')
)

lock <- if (lockfile_present) {
  jsonlite::fromJSON(lockfile_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)
} else {
  NULL
}
locked_r <- if (is.null(lock)) 'no lockfile' else lock$R$Version
locked_pkgs <- vapply(pkg_deps, function(p) {
  v <- lock$Packages[[p]]$Version
  if (is.null(v)) 'not locked' else v
}, character(1))

# The renderer does not export its version to the R session, so ask
# the quarto binary on the path; a failure is reported, not hidden.
quarto_version <- tryCatch(
  system2('quarto', '--version', stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)[1],
  error = function(e) NA_character_,
  warning = function(w) NA_character_
)
actual_r <- paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = '.')

colophon_rows <- tibble::tibble(
  field = c(
    'R version',
    'Platform',
    'Quarto version',
    paste('Package:', pkg_deps),
    'renv.lock present'
  ),
  actual = c(
    actual_r,
    R.version$platform,
    ifelse(is.na(quarto_version), 'not found', quarto_version),
    pkg_versions,
    ifelse(lockfile_present, 'yes', 'no')
  ),
  locked = c(
    locked_r,
    'not recorded',
    'not recorded',
    locked_pkgs,
    ''
  )
)

mismatch <- colophon_rows$field[
  colophon_rows$field %in% c('R version', paste('Package:', pkg_deps)) &
    colophon_rows$actual != colophon_rows$locked
]
executed_on <- format(Sys.Date(), '%Y-%m-%d')

knitr::kable(
  colophon_rows,
  col.names = c('Field', 'Actual', 'Locked')
)
```

The last row is the book's own honest reproducibility
disclosure, made the same way the book asks every analysis
to make it: by naming the artifact rather than asserting
the level. When this page last executed, an `renv.lock`
for the book's own source
`r if (lockfile_present) 'was present' else 'was absent'`,
so the table reports
'`r if (lockfile_present) 'yes' else 'no'`'. This
sentence and the table are computed in the same
execution, so they cannot disagree with each other. A
lockfile is the L1 artifact. The L2 step, a `Dockerfile`
that pins the operating system and the R runtime,
`r if (dockerfile_present) 'is also in place' else 'is not yet in place'`.

A lockfile records versions; it does not make the session
use them. `r if (length(mismatch) == 0) 'Every row the lockfile records agreed with the session that executed this page.' else paste0('In the session that executed this page, ', length(mismatch), if (length(mismatch) == 1) ' row' else ' rows', ' differed from the lockfile (', paste(sub('^Package: ', '', mismatch), collapse = ', '), '). Restoring the lockfile would reinstall the locked package versions but not R itself, which only a pinned environment, the L2 rung, fixes.')`

The HTML edition is the accessible one. Its pages are checked
with an automated accessibility tool, its figures carry alt text,
and its folded answers open from the keyboard. The PDF is not yet
a tagged PDF: we tried PDF/UA tagging and found that it is not
yet compatible with the line breaking that keeps long code lines
on the printed page, so a screen-reader user should prefer the
HTML.

This page last executed on `r executed_on`.
